stories.title: AEW Blood & Guts injury update | Exclusive
stories.tldr: Following the violent and bloody AEW Blood and Guts event on November 4, 2026, an exclusive report confirmed that no wrestlers sustained injuries from either the men or women matches. While there was initial concern regarding Darby Allin due to a tooth issue caused by his own knee during a bump, he was ultimately cleared. The event featured victories by The Brawling Birds, Harley Cameron, Kris Statlander, Willow Nightingale, and Queen Aminata in the women match, and The Don Callis Family in the men match.

stories.title: FTR vs. MCMG IV, Chris Jericho match announced for AEW Collision
stories.tldr: AEW has announced a loaded card for this Saturday's live episode of Collision, which emanates directly from Chris Jericho's Rock 'n' Wrestling Rager cruise ship. The marquee bouts feature the fourth installment of the thrilling best-of-five series between FTR and the Motor City Machine Guns, along with Chris Jericho facing Blake Christian. Additionally, fans will see Mina Shirakawa take on Persephone and an AEW National title match between Andrade El Idolo and Tommaso Ciampa.

stories.title: Result, key moments & spots from men’s AEW Blood & Guts match
stories.tldr: The Don Callis Family left Wednesday’s men’s AEW Blood & Guts match victorious after Adam Copeland was forced to surrender for his team — a move that didn’t save his teammate Darby Allin from a massive fall . Near the end of the match, the various Callis Family members had the Will Ospreay-led team

stories.title: AEW Men’s Blood & Guts 2026 Match Ends With Shocking Surrender
stories.tldr: The November 4 episode of Dynamite featured a brutal men Blood and Guts match between the Don Callis Family and a star-studded team led by Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland. Filled with dangerous spots, bloodshed, and weapons, the violent war came down to a dramatic final phase after Will Ospreay entered as the final participant. The match ultimately concluded in shocking fashion when the Don Callis Family cornered Adam Copeland and chained him by his throat, forcing a surrender rather than ending via traditional pinfall or submission.

stories.title: Darby Allin gets thrown off the top of the cage like Mankind after Cope quits Blood & Guts
stories.tldr: The men's Blood and Guts match main evented a recent episode of Dynamite, featuring Team Ospreay battling Team Callis inside the brutal steel structure. The chaotic war featured signature stunts, including Steven Borden taking a thumbtacks bump and Kazuchika Okada using a leaf blower to clear the ring. The match concluded when Adam Copeland was forced to surrender to save Will Ospreay from a vicious screwdriver attack by Kyle Fletcher. Following the submission, Wardlow sent Darby Allin crashing off the top of the cage in a terrifying moment, setting the stage for Full Gear.

stories.title: Don Callis Family Wins Men’s Blood & Guts After Adam Copeland Surrenders; Darby Allin Tossed From Top Of The Cage
stories.tldr: The Don Callis Family emerged victorious in a brutal Men's Blood and Guts match on AEW Dynamite after Adam Copeland was forced to surrender. The chaotic encounter featured extreme weapon usage, including barbed wire chairs, thumbtacks, and explosives. The climax saw Kyle Fletcher threaten Will Ospreay with a screwdriver, prompting Copeland's surrender to protect his teammate. Following the submission, Wardlow capped off the night by tossing Darby Allin from the top of the cage through a stack of tables at ringside.

stories.title: AEW Men’s Blood & Guts Ends In Chaos: Darby Allin Takes Horrifying Fall, More
stories.tldr: The men's Blood and Guts match on AEW Dynamite ended in extreme chaos as the Don Callis Family defeated their opponents after Adam Copeland was forced to surrender. The brutal double-ring steel cage encounter featured high-risk spots, thumbtacks, exploding chairs, and a pyrotechnic trap. Following the submission, Wardlow horrifyingly hurled Darby Allin from the roof of the cage through two stacked tables on the floor.

stories.title: Wardlow Throws Darby Allin Off Top of Cage to Close AEW Dynamite: Blood & Guts
stories.tldr: AEW Dynamite Blood and Guts concluded with a shocking and violent moment as Wardlow hurled Darby Allin from the top of the steel cage. Following a command from Kyle to do it, Wardlow showed no hesitation in sending Allin crashing through a stack of tables below. The brutal spot served as the final image of the broadcast, highlighting the extreme lengths Wardlow was willing to go to inflict damage. While Allin is known for putting his body on the line, this massive fall escalated the violence and instantly became the defining talking point of the show.

stories.title: Two developments for AEW Full Gear 2026 card
stories.tldr: Wednesday's Blood and Guts edition of AEW Dynamite set up two major additions for the upcoming Full Gear pay-per-view card in Phoenix. Following a chaotic brawl, Hangman Page reluctantly agreed to a Texas Death Match to defend the AEW Trios titles alongside Brody King and Bandido against Swerve Strickland, Kofi, and Austin Creed. Additionally, Jon Moxley held an uneasy sit-down meeting to recruit Orange Cassidy, Kyle O'Reilly, and Roderick Strong of The Conglomeration for the upcoming Anarchy in the Arena match. The updated lineup for next Saturday's event features several high-profile championship bouts alongside these newly confirmed stipulations.

stories.title: Adam Page Finally Agrees to Texas Deathmatch at AEW Full Gear 2026
stories.tldr: Adam Page has finally agreed to step into a Texas Deathmatch at AEW Full Gear after weeks of resisting the stipulation. During the November 4 episode of AEW Dynamite Blood and Guts, Bandido convinced Page to accept the match to finally address the ongoing disrespect and violence from Swerve Strickland and New Level. Shortly after their backstage conversation, Tony Khan and the AEW commentary team officially confirmed the high stakes clash for the upcoming pay per view. This violent stipulation sets the stage for a brutal chapter in the bitter rivalry between these fierce competitors.

stories.title: Result & key moments from a bloody AEW women’s Blood & Guts match
stories.tldr: The 2026 women’s Blood and Guts match delivered a violent and bloody spectacle on AEW Dynamite, culminating in Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron forcing a submission from Julia Hart. The grueling near hourlong double cage match featured numerous brutal spots, including Megan Bayne becoming the first woman to bleed heavily and a bizarre incident involving a barbed wire 2x4 stuck in Skye Blue. Following their victory, Statlander and Cameron earned a shot at the AEW Women’s World Tag Team titles currently held by Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor at Full Gear.

stories.title: FTR vs. Motor City Machine Guns IV, Persephone Bout, More Set For 11/7 AEW Collision
stories.tldr: The upcoming November 7 episode of AEW Collision features a stacked lineup highlighted by the fourth installment of the best-of-five series between FTR and the Motor City Machine Guns. Holding a 2-1 advantage, the Machine Guns can clinch the series victory if they defeat Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler. The card also features Persephone facing Mina Shirakawa, Chris Jericho taking on Blake Christian, and Tommaso Ciampa challenging Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship.

stories.title: Adam Page & Brodido To Face New Level & Swerve Strickland In Texas Deathmatch At AEW Full Gear
stories.tldr: Adam Page has finally agreed to step into a Texas Deathmatch after weeks of resisting the violent stipulations brought to him by Swerve Strickland and New Level. Following another brutal backstage encounter, Bandido convinced Page to join forces with him to put an end to the ongoing disrespect shown by Strickland. Tony Khan and the commentary team officially confirmed the high-stakes match for the upcoming AEW Full Gear pay-per-view. Fans can look forward to full live coverage and post-show reviews as the feud reaches its boiling point.

stories.title: Hangman Page Gives In, 'Texas Death' Official For AEW Full Gear
stories.tldr: The AEW World Trios Championships will be defended in a brutal Texas Death match at AEW Full Gear 2026 after champions Hangman Adam Page, Brody King, and Bandido officially accepted the challenge. Page initially resisted the stipulation due to his violent history with Swerve Strickland in similar matches, but relented after Strickland abducted and bloodied Bandido. Following another chaotic backstage brawl involving Kofi and Austin Creed, Bandido and King convinced a reluctant Page to agree to the terms.

stories.title: AEW women go insane with ultra hardcore violence in weapons-filled Blood & Guts match
stories.tldr: The November 4 episode of AEW Dynamite opened with a brutal women's Blood & Guts match featuring a massive arsenal of hardcore weapons. Heels gained the early advantage as both teams clashed inside and outside the double rings with fluorescent light tubes, barbed wire, and glass shards. The chaotic war escalated with high-risk table spots and heavy bloodshed before reaching the match beyond phase.

stories.title: AEW Women’s Blood & Guts Match Ends In Brutal Fashion On Dynamite
stories.tldr: The women of All Elite Wrestling delivered a violent and historic Blood and Guts match on the November 4, 2026 episode of Dynamite in Jacksonville, Florida. The brutal encounter featured barbed wire, light tubes, broken glass, toy bricks, and a massive splash off the top of the cage through a table. The grueling war ended when Kris Statlander wrapped barbed wire around Julia Hart's face to force a submission, giving the winning team major momentum heading into the Full Gear pay-per-view.

stories.title: Julia Hart Submits in Brutal Finish to AEW Women’s Blood & Guts Match
stories.tldr: AEWs women's Blood and Guts match delivered extreme violence on November 4, 2026, featuring heavy weaponry, broken glass, and multiple bleeding competitors inside the steel cage. The grueling war came to an end when Harley Cameron locked Julia Hart in a single-leg crab while Kris Statlander tortured her with barbed wire across the mouth. This brutal combination forced Hart to tap out, handing the victory to Statlander, Cameron, Willow Nightingale, Queen Aminata, Jamie Hayter, and Alex Windsor.

stories.title: Steven Borden on Whether He Would Ever Wear His Father Sting’s Iconic Face Paint
stories.tldr: Steven Borden is currently not planning to wear his father Sting's iconic face paint or use his signature gear in his wrestling career. During a recent interview, Borden explained that he wants to establish his own identity rather than immediately relying on his father's legacy. His tag team partner Darby Allin agrees, noting that any tribute must feel genuine rather than coming across as a cheap imitation. While Borden is taking things week by week to carve out his own path, he is leaving the door open for potential callbacks in the future when the timing is right.

stories.title: Mustafa Ali’s TNA Wrestling Contract Set to Expire at End of 2026
stories.tldr: Mustafa Ali is heading toward free agency as his current TNA Wrestling contract is set to expire at the end of 2026. Beyond his on-screen success and mentoring of Jason Hotch, Ali has been informally scouting independent talent and passing recommendations to management. Because he is highly regarded behind the scenes, TNA is expected to offer him a new deal before his contract officially concludes. Fans and management will soon find out whether he chooses to stay or explore other wrestling promotions.

stories.title: Pro Wrestling’s Villainous Politician Just Became a Mayor in Rhode Island
stories.tldr: Rhode Island state representative and independent professional wrestler David Morales has been elected as the 40th mayor of Providence, winning roughly 81 percent of the vote against Republican Dave Talan. At 28 years old, the Democrat will become the youngest mayor in the city's history when he takes office in January 2027. Outside of his political career, Morales has famously performed since 2021 as The Commissioner, an arrogant, corrupt authority figure for the Renegade Wrestling Alliance. Although he stepped away from regular in-ring competition to focus on his campaign, Morales has refused to rule out a future return to wrestling, famously noting that in this world, fans should never say never.

stories.title: Ricochet says the dirt sheets have it all wrong about AEW’s awesome locker room
stories.tldr: Ricochet recently addressed ongoing rumors from wrestling dirt sheets regarding backstage morale in All Elite Wrestling. During a recent interview, the high-flying star maintained that the locker room environment is actually fantastic and drastically different from what is reported online. He praised his colleagues for putting their egos aside and working collaboratively to improve the overall product. According to Ricochet, this selfless attitude among the vast majority of the roster has directly contributed to the higher quality of recent television shows.

stories.title: AEW's Kyle Fletcher Blames 'Doo-Doo Head' Partner For WrestleDream Loss
stories.tldr: Following an unsuccessful bid for the AEW World Tag Team Championships against the Young Bucks at WrestleDream, Kyle Fletcher publicly blamed his tag team partner Kevin Knight for the loss. In a post-match YouTube vlog filmed poolside, Fletcher jokingly referred to Knight as a stupid doo-doo head and criticized him for blowing the match after Knight tagged himself in at a crucial moment. Despite the playful jab and past friction between the two before being paired by Don Callis, Fletcher moves forward to challenge Will Ospreay for the AEW Men's World Championship at Full Gear.

stories.title: Booker T says Cody Rhodes and Matt Cardona didn’t fit in AEW because they are “entertainment wrestlers”
stories.tldr: During a recent podcast episode, WWE Hall of Famer Booker T discussed the stylistic differences between AEW and WWE. He explained that foundational AEW wrestlers view the business differently than traditional entertainment-focused veterans like The Rock, Stone Cold Steve Austin, and Kurt Angle. According to Booker T, this ideological divide is why stars like Cody Rhodes and Matt Cardona ultimately did not fit in the promotion. He also noted that even newly arrived acts like The Hurt Syndicate can experience cooling periods within the unique AEW environment.

stories.title: Taya Valkyrie Announces AEW Departure, Says She Turned Down Contract Extension
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has announced her departure from All Elite Wrestling after more than three years with the promotion. She revealed that she turned down a contract extension offer to test the free agent market and pursue new opportunities in wrestling, television, and creative fields. Valkyrie expressed gratitude for her time in the company, her colleagues, and the fans while reflecting on an extensive career that spans major promotions worldwide.

stories.title: Taya Valkyrie Announces AEW Departure After Turning Down Contract Extension
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has officially become a free agent after declining an offer to extend her contract with All Elite Wrestling. In a statement released by her team, she expressed deep gratitude for her time in the promotion, the relationships she built, and the unwavering support of the fans. Valkyrie is now looking forward to exploring new opportunities in professional wrestling, television, and music as she begins this next chapter of her multifaceted career.

stories.title: Steven Borden Explains Why He Hasn’t Adopted Sting’s Iconic Look In AEW
stories.tldr: Steven Borden recently addressed why he has chosen not to use his father Sting's iconic face paint and persona during his early run in AEW. Teaming up with Darby Allin, Borden explained that immediately copying his father's legendary look could have sparked negative fan backlash and set unrealistic expectations. Instead, Borden is focusing on building his own unique identity in the wrestling industry on a week by week basis. Allin also chimed in during the interview to emphasize the importance of staying true to oneself rather than compromising beliefs for success.

stories.title: Rob Van Dam Criticizes Modern Wrestling And AEW’s In-Ring Style
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Rob Van Dam recently criticized modern professional wrestling and AEW's in-ring style for prioritizing overly complicated sequences over believable competition. Speaking on a recent podcast, RVD argued that lengthy move setups expose the business and make matches resemble backyard wrestling due to excessive creative freedom. In contrast, he praised WWE for focusing on storytelling, simplicity, and structured matches that make sense. Van Dam also dismissed extreme elements like burning houses or self-mutilation, defending his longstanding consistency against accusations of hypocrisy.

stories.title: AEW wrestler leaves company after declining contract extension
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has officially entered free agency after deciding not to accept an offer to extend her contract with All Elite Wrestling. Having debuted with the company in March 2023, she released a statement expressing gratitude for her time there and excitement for her future. She is now looking forward to exploring new opportunities as a wrestler, television personality, and creative.

stories.title: AEW departure confirmed: Taya Valkyrie enters free agency after turning down contract extension offer
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has officially confirmed her departure from All Elite Wrestling after turning down a contract extension offer, making her a free agent. In a statement, she expressed gratitude for her time with the company, her colleagues, and the fans while looking forward to new opportunities in wrestling, television, and creative fields. Valkyrie joined AEW in March 2023, primarily featuring on Ring of Honor in recent times, and departs with an extensive resume that includes historic championship reigns in TNA and AAA.

stories.title: Former Knockouts & AAA champ declines contract extension with AEW
stories.tldr: Former Knockouts and AAA champion Taya Valkyrie has officially entered free agency after declining an offer to extend her contract with All Elite Wrestling. In a statement released on social media, the 43-year-old veteran expressed gratitude for her three-year run with the company and the relationships she built during her time there. Valkyrie now looks forward to exploring new opportunities in wrestling, television, and creative projects, alongside her recent ventures in reality television and music.

stories.title: Taya Valkyrie Turns Down AEW Offer, Leaves The Company
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has officially departed All Elite Wrestling after choosing not to accept a contract extension offer from the promotion. Entering free agency, the veteran wrestler expressed gratitude for her time in the company, her colleagues, and the fans who supported her run. She plans to remain active in professional wrestling while also pursuing new ventures as a television personality and creative force.

stories.title: Taya Valkyrie announces her departure from AEW
stories.tldr: Taya Valkyrie has officially announced her departure from All Elite Wrestling after choosing not to accept a contract extension with the company. Entering free agency, she expressed gratitude for her time with the organization, the talent she worked with, and the support of the fans. Valkyrie is now looking forward to exploring new opportunities in wrestling, television, and creative projects, building on recent ventures like appearing on Traitors Canada and releasing her debut music EP.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite ticket sales ahead of tonight’s show (11-04-2026)
stories.tldr: AEW Dynamite is broadcasting live tonight from the VyStar Veterans Memorial Arena in Jacksonville, Florida, marking the company's debut in the venue with roughly 4,348 tickets distributed so far. The event has seen a recent surge of 421 newly distributed tickets over the past day, though it faces major television competition. Tonight's show goes head-to-head with a stacked, main-roster-heavy edition of WWE NXT on the CW network featuring John Cena and CM Punk. Meanwhile, the AEW card is highlighted by high-stakes Men's and Women's Blood and Guts matches.

stories.title: RVD Says AEW Wrestlers Have Too Much Creative Control, Criticizes Jon Moxley’s Weapon Usage
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Rob Van Dam recently criticized AEW's creative approach, arguing that wrestlers have too much control and comparing the product to backyard wrestling. He took specific issue with Jon Moxley's weapon usage and other extreme elements like staple use and burning houses. RVD also criticized modern wrestling matches that feature overly choreographed setups that expose the business, despite having made several guest appearances for AEW in the past.

stories.title: Update On Steven Borden Jr. Possibly Using Sting-Inspired Face Paint In AEW
stories.tldr: Steven Borden Jr. is currently focusing on building his own wrestling identity in AEW alongside tag team partner Darby Allin, rather than immediately adopting his father Sting's iconic face paint and persona. Borden noted that using the legendary look right away would have felt like playing the greatest hits and could have backfired with fans. Meanwhile, Allin emphasized the importance of staying true to oneself in the wrestling business without compromising personal beliefs for success. Allin hopes his journey to the top of AEW without changing his core identity will inspire the next generation of wrestlers.

stories.title: Danhausen calls out “clickbait losers” for sharing a quote from him out of context
stories.tldr: Danhausen recently appeared on an interview with Chris Van Vliet to discuss trademarking his signature face paint after noticing its resemblance to a Magic: The Gathering card. A media outlet shared a clipped quote on social media that provoked fan backlash, prompting the wrestling star to angrily address the situation. Danhausen criticized the publication for clickbait tactics and shared the full context of his remarks. He clarified that he loves the card game, has never planned to sue anyone, and simply secured the trademark to protect his own creative work.

stories.title: Rob Van Dam on Jon Moxley’s weapon usage and AEW’s creative freedom: ‘The inmates are running the asylum’
stories.tldr: Hall of fame wrestler Rob Van Dam defended himself against accusations of hypocrisy after previously criticizing All Elite Wrestling for its booking and Jon Moxley's extreme weapon usage. Speaking on Wrestling with Rip Rogers, RVD compared Moxley's spiked club to his own ridiculous 2010 TNA write-off involving Abyss and a nail-studded plank called Janice. He argued that AEW suffers from the inmates running the asylum because wrestlers have too much creative control, leading to an amateurish, backyard-style product that contrasts with WWE's more structured storytelling. Furthermore, Van Dam criticized modern performers for relying on overly complex setups that expose the business by killing the competitive feel of a match.

stories.title: Kurt Angle’s words of encouragement to a fan: “It’s okay to suck sometimes”
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Kurt Angle recently shared an encouraging and humorous video message for a fan who recently came out of the closet. Blending genuine support with his iconic wrestling persona, Angle told the fan to always be true to themselves. He famously adapted his catchphrase to note that it is okay to suck sometimes, provided they do it with his signature values.

stories.title: AEW Star Ilja Dragunov Spotted Training At Japanese Wrestling Dojo
stories.tldr: AEW star Ilja Dragunov was recently spotted expanding his craft during a visit to Japan by training at the Sendai Girls Pro Wrestling dojo. The intensive two-hour session featured technical drills and sparring alongside promotion roster members, including Chihiro Hashimoto. Dragunov also shares a personal connection to the all-women promotion through his significant other, Lady Leigh, who has been competing there since September after previously wrestling in WWE as Jin Tala.

stories.title: Rob Van Dam on the AEW product: “I think the inmates are running the asylum”
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Rob Van Dam recently shared his criticisms of the modern professional wrestling landscape during an appearance with Rip Rogers. RVD specifically targeted AEW, using the phrase that the inmates are running the asylum to describe the high level of creative control given to the wrestlers. He contrasted this style with WWE's more structured storytelling and expressed his dislike for overly complicated setups and dangerous stunts that he feels expose the business.

stories.title: Darby Allin Recalls Painful Drive Home After AEW Blood & Guts Fire Spot
stories.tldr: Darby Allin recently reflected on the grueling aftermath of his infamous flaming table spot from last year's AEW Blood and Guts match. Appearing on Going Ringside alongside Steven Borden, Allin detailed the painful four-to-six-hour car ride home with his severely burned back pressed against nothing. With the AC blasting and enduring agonizing pain, Allin's firsthand experience highlights the brutal reality of these high-stakes live television stunts. Both Allin and Borden are now scheduled for the upcoming November 4 Blood and Guts match.

stories.title: Official Wrestle Kingdom matches include one that could ‘entirely’ change NJPW/AEW relationship
stories.tldr: Following the Power Struggle fallout, New Japan Pro Wrestling has officially confirmed the first seven matches for Wrestle Kingdom 21. The card features high-profile bouts including Kenny Omega challenging Yota Tsuji for the IWGP Heavyweight title and an Unbound Death Match between Jon Moxley and Shingo Takagi. Tsuji notably stated that his main event clash with Omega could entirely change the dynamic of the NJPW and AEW relationship.

stories.title: Mercedes Moné hits like a ‘p***y a** b**ch’
stories.tldr: Marina Shafir and Mercedes Mone are officially colliding for the AEW women’s world title at Full Gear. The rivalry heated up significantly when Shafir confronted the champion on Dynamite to insult her in-ring striking power. The verbal exchange quickly erupted into a physical brawl featuring a title belt assault.

stories.title: Max Caster Addresses His Future, Following Hiatus Announcement
stories.tldr: Following his controversial appearance and subsequent hiatus announcement, Max Caster addressed his professional future during a virtual signing. Caster stated that he is currently turning down all wrestling bookings, confirming that this virtual signing would be his final wrestling-related appearance for the foreseeable future. While he refused to rule out a future return to the ring by noting you never say never, he provided no timeline for how long his break will last. During the session, he also expressed skepticism regarding the current status of his former tag team partner, Anthony Bowens.

stories.title: Darby Allin shares one regret about New York City Marathon
stories.tldr: Darby Allin recently completed his first New York City Marathon with a finishing time of 5:35:14. However, he now admits he regrets running the grueling 26.2 miles with zero training. The lack of preparation is causing major physical issues as he prepares for tonight's violent Blood and Guts match in AEW. Allin explains that extreme pursuits like this and climbing Mount Everest happen through spontaneous decision making rather than long-term planning.

stories.title: Steven Borden details scary concussion suffered at AEW All Out 2026
stories.tldr: Steven Borden recently opened up about the terrifying concussion he suffered during a tag team match at AEW All Out on September 26, 2026, which required the referee to stop the match live on pay-per-view. While Borden casually claimed he was knocked out for a little bit, his partner Darby Allin revealed that Borden was actually snoring in the ring for six straight minutes. Despite the severity of the injury, Borden found the recovery frustrating because he physically felt fine, but he has since returned to action and is heading straight into a violent Blood & Guts match.

stories.title: AEW Senior Vice President Justin Street leaves company to return to TKO
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling has lost a key executive with the departure of Justin Street, who served as the Senior Vice President of Corporate Partnerships and Sales. Street exited the promotion in October after a tenure that lasted approximately one year following his start in January 2025. Following his departure from Tony Khan's company, Street returned to Professional Bull Riders, an organization owned by TKO Group Holdings, which is also the parent company of WWE and UFC. Prior to joining AEW, Street spent seven years with Professional Bull Riders, eventually rising to the position of Senior Vice President of Corporate Partnerships and Media Sales.

stories.title: Will Ospreay accepts Callum Newman's challenge for NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21
stories.tldr: AEW star Will Ospreay has officially accepted a challenge from United Empire stablemate Callum Newman for a one-on-one match at NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 on January 4, 2027. The match was made after tensions boiled over during their unsuccessful IWGP Tag Team Title match against the Knockout Brothers in Hiroshima, where Newman was disqualified for using a chair and the two subsequently brawled. Ospreay released a public statement expressing embarrassment over the incident and requested that other United Empire members stay out of the upcoming Tokyo Dome bout so he and Newman can settle their differences cleanly.

stories.title: MJF set to make NJPW debut at Wrestle Kingdom 21 against G1 Climax winner
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF is set to make his professional wrestling debut in Japan at New Japan Pro-Wrestling Wrestle Kingdom 21 on January 4, 2027. Following a video challenge aired during the NJPW Power Struggle event, MJF challenged 2026 G1 Climax winner Ryohei Oiwa to a match at the Tokyo Dome, boasting that he would defeat him with a simple headlock takeover. Oiwa accepted the challenge, setting up a marquee cross-promotional bout despite NJPW not yet officially finalizing the lineup.

stories.title: Death Riders declare war on NJPW ahead of Wrestle Kingdom 21
stories.tldr: New Japan Pro Wrestling's Power Struggle event set the stage for a massive crossover showing at Wrestle Kingdom 21 with heavy AEW involvement. MJF challenged Ryohei Oiwa, Will Ospreay booked a match against Callum Newman, and Kenny Omega staked a claim for the IWGP Heavyweight title. Meanwhile, Gabe Kidd and the Death Riders officially declared war on New Japan by assaulting Hiroshi Tanahashi, Yuya Uemura, and Shingo Takagi after a chaotic night of action.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland Booked for Indie Match
stories.tldr: Former AEW World Champion Swerve Strickland is returning to the independent wrestling scene for the first time in two years. He is scheduled to face Ninja Mack at the Fourth Rope Heelmatic event, a collaborative show with Mass Appeal founded by rapper Westside Gunn at the Melrose Ballroom in New York City on Thursday, November 12. This rare indie appearance occurs just days before Strickland teams up with Austin Creed and Kofi to challenge for the AEW Trios Championship at the Full Gear pay-per-view on Saturday, November 14.

stories.title: Ricochet Reflects on Emotional AEW Tribute Match for PAC
stories.tldr: Ricochet recently reflected on the emotional September 30 episode of AEW Dynamite, where he wrestled Will Ospreay in a tribute match honoring their late friend PAC. He explained that having the match to focus on provided a necessary distraction from the grief following PAC's sudden passing at the age of forty. Despite having very little time to put the bout together, the two performers relied on their deep history and close friendship with PAC to deliver a meaningful performance. Ospreay ultimately won the match at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh by hitting PAC's signature Black Arrow.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes Names Strongest Opponents He Has Faced
stories.tldr: During a recent appearance on the Double Coverage Podcast, undisputed wrestling star Cody Rhodes named the toughest and strongest opponents he has ever faced in the ring. He highlighted legendary powerhouses like Mark Henry and Big Show, alongside current standouts such as Big E, Claudio Castagnoli, John Cena, and Bron Breakker. Rhodes also detailed the terrifying speed of Brock Lesnar and praised Bianca Belair as arguably WWE greatest athlete ever.

stories.title: Ricochet Discusses His Performer Growth in AEW
stories.tldr: Ricochet believes he is a stronger performer now in AEW than during earlier stages of his career. He credits this growth to developing a deep emotional connection with fans rather than relying solely on spectacular physical moves. This evolution is prominently displayed through his current heel run, where he actively embraces drawing negative crowd reactions to elevate his opponents.

stories.title: Bryce Remsburg Suggests AEW Could Hold Stadium Show in Philadelphia
stories.tldr: AEW referee Bryce Remsburg recently discussed the possibility of the promotion hosting a major stadium show at Lincoln Financial Field, the home of the NFL's Philadelphia Eagles. While noting that Philadelphia is one of AEW's strongest markets and that the venue has previous experience hosting WrestleMania, Remsburg admitted that current demand might not quite support a stadium show there just yet. He did not rule out the possibility for the future, even as separate rumors point toward a potential AEW stadium show happening in New York City this coming April.

stories.title: Paul Wight Praises AEW's Kyle Fletcher
stories.tldr: AEW commentator Paul Wight recently named Kyle Fletcher as the wrestler who impresses him the most due to his incredible momentum and massive star potential. Wight praised Fletcher for checking every box in the industry, highlighting his in-ring skills, promo ability, work ethic, and professional backstage demeanor. Calling him a very humble and good kid, Wight ultimately stated that Fletcher has money written all on him.

stories.title: Gabe Kidd Takes Shot at WWE Roster
stories.tldr: AEW star Gabe Kidd recently dismissed the entire WWE roster during an Instagram Q and A session while waiting for a connecting flight. When asked about a dream match against any WWE superstar, Kidd bluntly stated that none of them interest him and that they are all shit. This trademark controversy comes as Kidd also navigates major changes in his own career, including former stablemates David Finlay and Clark Connors turning on him to form a new faction called The Cut with The Bang Bang Gang.

stories.title: Update on AEW and Skydance Media Rights Situation
stories.tldr: Dave Meltzer has provided a fresh subscriber-only update regarding the ongoing discussions between AEW and Skydance. While previous reports questioned whether the media company would exercise an option year, this new report delves deeper into the current backstage dynamics and negotiations. Subscribers received a comprehensive breakdown of how these talks are progressing behind the scenes. The latest analysis sheds more light on what the potential partnership could mean for AEW's television future.

stories.title: Darby Allin completes the New York City Marathon
stories.tldr: AEW star Darby Allin successfully completed the New York City Marathon with a time of 5:34:34 after refusing to do any training for the race. The grueling endurance feat came just days after he wrestled Hechicero in Mexico City and adds to an extraordinary athletic resume that includes climbing Mount Everest. Allin will now pivot immediately back to professional wrestling to compete in the upcoming Blood and Guts match.

stories.title: Mansoor comments on AEW benched wrestlers taking outside opportunities
stories.tldr: AEW star Mansoor recently discussed the realities of being benched in the professional wrestling industry during a candid interview. He argued that wrestlers under guaranteed contracts have no excuse not to pursue outside bookings when they are not being actively used on television. Mansoor highlighted his own bustling international schedule, including upcoming dates with DDT in Japan and past tours with CMLL and in India, while praising AEW leadership for allowing such flexibility. Ultimately, he believes that having a guaranteed deal while still being able to work globally is an incredible privilege that leaves no room for complaints.

stories.title: Ric Flair responds to questions about how he is still alive
stories.tldr: Ric Flair has issued a blunt response to people questioning how he is still alive following a recent fall in Florida that resulted in facial and eye injuries. The two-time WWE Hall of Famer pointed to the immense physical toll of his legendary career, including thousands of matches, a 1975 plane crash, and a near-fatal medical emergency. Flair emphasized that a minor fall is nothing compared to the severe trauma his body has successfully endured and survived over the decades. His remarks highlight his lifelong resilience amidst ongoing health challenges, such as a current blood clot and upcoming surgeries.

stories.title: John Cena Classic scheduling could compete with AEW Worlds End
stories.tldr: The mystery surrounding the upcoming John Cena Classic tournament may soon be solved, with wrestling observer Dave Meltzer pointing to December 19 as the frontrunner date based on WWE's crowded winter schedule. If this date is locked in, Cena's special event would run directly head-to-head against All Elite Wrestling's major pay-per-view, Worlds End. Fans will not have to wait long for official confirmation, as John Cena is scheduled to appear on the November 2 episode of Raw in Brooklyn to finally reveal all the details.

stories.title: Thunder Rosa reflects on emotional CMLL Grand Prix appearance
stories.tldr: AEW star Thunder Rosa recently opened up about getting emotional and crying during her first appearance at the CMLL Women's Grand Prix in Mexico. Competing as part of Team CMLL, Rosa was overwhelmed with national pride upon hearing the Mexican national anthem before the matches even began. Although she initially found it slightly unusual to represent CMLL, she quickly embraced the role given her status as a champion with the promotion. While Skadi ultimately secured the tournament victory for the team, Rosa walked away with a deeply personal and unforgettable career memory.

stories.title: Mina Shirakawa comments on confidence without holding a championship
stories.tldr: AEW star Mina Shirakawa recently admitted that going months without holding a championship has taken a toll on her self-confidence. However, her perspective shifted when CMLL Japan Women's Champion India Sioux personally selected her as an opponent for an upcoming international match. This vote of confidence revitalized Shirakawa, motivating her to shine on a global stage once again. She ultimately capitalized on this opportunity by defeating India Sioux at CMLL's Rey del Inframundo event on October 30.

stories.title: Will Ospreay credits WCW influence on his wrestling style
stories.tldr: AEW World Champion Will Ospreay recently credited the WCW cruiserweight division as a major influence on his high-flying wrestling style. Speaking ahead of AEW WrestleDream 2026, Ospreay shared how studying cruiserweight tapes on a backyard trampoline and eventually a backyard wrestling ring helped him hone his craft as a youth. Despite modifying his style following neck surgery in September 2025, he successfully captured the AEW World Championship at Wembley Stadium at AEW All In London 2026.

stories.title: Backstage update on Toni Storm's AEW return plans
stories.tldr: Toni Storm's anticipated AEW return may be delayed further than initially expected. Backstage reports indicate she is still not slated to step back into the ring before the end of the year. Additionally, creative plans regarding the identity of her mystery attacker remain fluid. While an initial idea was pitched when the angle began, officials may change direction before she finally comes back.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite scheduled not to air head-to-head with WWE SmackDown on New Year's Day
stories.tldr: Initial reports indicated that WWE SmackDown and AEW Dynamite would clash on New Year's Day. However, scheduling adjustments ensure the two programs will not air head-to-head. AEW Dynamite will instead broadcast in an afternoon time slot following the college football playoffs.

stories.title: Andrade to defend AEW National Title on Jericho Cruise
stories.tldr: Andrade El Idolo will defend the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa in a high-stakes rematch following their acclaimed WrestleDream encounter. The title bout is now officially confirmed to take place on a special upcoming episode of AEW Collision airing live from the Chris Jericho Rock 'N' Wrestling Rager at Sea. Ciampa earned this latest opportunity following a recent television victory, setting the stage for what will be Andrade's ninth defense of the championship.

stories.title: Wrestlers added to AEW Women's Blood & Guts match
stories.tldr: AEW has finalized the lineups for the upcoming women's Blood & Guts match by adding newly crowned TBS Champion Queen Aminata and former titleholder Persephone to opposing sides. Persephone demanded a rematch and challenged Aminata to fill the final open slots on their respective teams following a surprise title change on Dynamite. The six-on-six clash will air live on Wednesday, November 4, amid critiques regarding the familiar faces and rushed build for the women's war.

stories.title: Mercedes Mone vs Marina Shafir set for AEW Full Gear
stories.tldr: Marina Shafir has officially earned a shot at the AEW Women’s World Championship, where she will challenge titleholder Mercedes Mone at the upcoming AEW Full Gear pay-per-view. The high-stakes match was made official following escalating tensions between the two competitors on recent episodes of Dynamite and Collision. The rivalry intensified when Shafir called out the champion and withstood a flurry of slaps without flinching, setting the stage for their upcoming championship clash on November 14 in Phoenix, Arizona.

stories.title: Andrade vs Tommaso Ciampa AEW National Title rematch set for Collision
stories.tldr: Andrade El Idolo will defend the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa in a high-stakes rematch on the upcoming episode of AEW Collision. The match stems from their critically acclaimed encounter at AEW WrestleDream where Andrade successfully retained his title. Ciampa subsequently earned another title opportunity after attacking the champion and scoring an impressive victory on television. This special edition of Collision will emanate live from Chris Jericho's Rock N Wrestling Rager cruise while docked in Miami, Florida.

stories.title: Samoa Joe teases changes to The Opps on AEW Collision
stories.tldr: Samoa Joe recently hinted at major changes within The Opps during a backstage promo on AEW Collision, appearing to question HOOK's leadership during Joe's recent absence. Joe addressed a shift in the group's perception and warned the AEW roster that the dynamic of the faction is about to change. Notably, group members Anthony Bowens and Action Andretti were absent from the segment.

stories.title: Adam Copeland on wrestling in Maple Leaf Gardens vs Wembley
stories.tldr: AEW star Adam Copeland recently revealed that wrestling at Maple Leaf Gardens meant more to him than performing at any other venue in the world, including Wembley Stadium. Growing up watching wrestling at the historic arena, Copeland thought stepping into its ring was an impossible dream, especially after his nine-year retirement. However, a collaborative effort with Scott D'Amore made the appearance possible following Copeland's transition to AEW. With his retirement officially set for 2027, Copeland has nearly completed his career bucket list, with only the Tokyo Dome left as a potential final milestone.

stories.title: Jake Roberts advises Tony Khan to loosen the reins in AEW
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Jake Roberts recently discussed his current career status and shared his thoughts on the creative direction of All Elite Wrestling. Now re-signed with WWE and enjoying life, Roberts praised AEW President Tony Khan as a sweet guy but suggested that he needs to loosen the reins and take more advice. Roberts also expressed his fondness for working with Lance Archer, calling their pairing perfect and stating that Archer is an unbelievable talent who never got the break he deserved.

stories.title: Anthony Bowens dresses as Max Caster for Halloween
stories.tldr: Anthony Bowens celebrated Halloween by sharing a humorous video impersonating his former tag team partner, Max Caster, complete with a fake mustache, microphone, and signature catchphrases. The lighthearted impersonation comes at an interesting time given their history in The Acclaimed and Caster recently stepping away from wrestling following a TNA controversy. Despite the recent backstage drama surrounding Caster, Bowens kept the tribute purely comedic and committed fully to the bit.

stories.title: Bryce Remsburg compares refereeing in indies vs AEW
stories.tldr: AEW referee Bryce Remsburg recently discussed the major adjustments he had to make transitioning from the independent circuit to television wrestling. Having spent 17 years refereeing on the indies, Remsburg described joining AEW in 2019 as moving from a bachelor's degree to a master's program. The biggest challenge was adapting to wearing an earpiece to receive live instructions from producers, agents, and Tony Khan. He noted that the empty arena era during the COVID-19 pandemic ultimately helped him gain the confidence needed to master television refereeing.

stories.title: Chris Jericho reacts to cameo role in Dexter: Resurrection
stories.tldr: AEW star Chris Jericho made a surprise cameo in the season two premiere of Dexter: Resurrection as a serial killer named Emmett Bell, also known as the Midnight Mangler. Jericho expressed his excitement about joining the show on Facebook while jokingly complaining that his character was robbed because Dexter Morgan ambushed him from behind. The new season, which features a star-studded cast including Michael C. Hall, Brian Cox, and Uma Thurman, airs weekly through January 2027. Meanwhile, Jericho is scheduled to appear on AEW Collision live from his upcoming wrestling cruise in November 2026.

stories.title: Orange Cassidy details worst injury of his career
stories.tldr: AEW star Orange Cassidy recently revealed the most severe injuries of his professional wrestling career during an appearance on The Rizzuto Show. He detailed a terrifying incident where a knee to the face broke his orbital bone and sinus cavity, causing him to vomit blood because it drained into his stomach. Cassidy also recounted a separate, bizarre shoulder dislocation where the joint was driven into his body, requiring general anesthesia and multiple medical staff to pull it back into place.

stories.title: Billy Gunn comments on his sons following his pro wrestling footsteps
stories.tldr: AEW star Billy Gunn recently opened up about the unique experience of sharing the wrestling industry with his sons, Austin and Colten Gunn. During an interview with Inside The Ropes, Gunn discussed their contrasting personalities, how their memorable betrayal storyline came together, and his initial reluctance for them to enter the business. Despite wanting them to pursue other paths, he ultimately gave his blessing after they completed their education and proved their natural talent in the ring.

stories.title: Darby Allin pays tribute to PAC at CMLL event
stories.tldr: Darby Allin recently made his much-anticipated CMLL debut in Mexico. During his marquee match against Hechicero, Allin paid a touching tribute to the late PAC by carrying a custom skateboard. Ultimately, Hechicero defeated the AEW star to exact revenge for their previous encounter on AEW Dynamite.
